29.23: Proud people will be disgraced; those who are humble will be respected.
29.24: Those who help thieves [to steal] only hurt themselves; [when they are in court], they solemnly ask [God] to curse them [if they do not tell the truth], but they do not tell the truth [about the crime that was committed], [and as a result, God will curse them].
29.25: It is [like] a dangerous trap [for people] to be ◄afraid of/worried about► what others will think about them, but those who trust in Yahweh are safe/protected.
29.26: Many [people] request rulers to do things to help them, but Yahweh is [the only one] who surely does for people what is fair/just.
29.27: Righteous [people] hate/detest those who do what is evil, and wicked [people] hate [those whose behavior is always] good.

30.1: These are sayings/messages that God gave to Agur, the son of Jakeh. [Agur wrote them] for Ithiel and Ucal.
30.2: It seems that I am very stupid; I do not deserve to be considered to be a human; I do not have the good sense that humans should have.
30.3: I have not learned [how to become] wise and I do not know [much] about God.
30.4: [But let me say this]: No one has ascended to heaven [to find out what God is like] and returned [to tell us]. No one has gathered/held the wind in his hand. No one has wrapped the water [in the ocean] in [a piece of] cloth, and no one has established the boundaries of the earth. [If you know who has done those things, tell me] his name, and the names of his children ! [But you do not know who has done those things, so you cannot speak with authority about what God is like].
30.5: Everything that God has said is true; he is [like] a shield for all those who request him to protect them.
30.6: Do not add to (OR, change) what God has said; if you do that, he will rebuke you and show that you are lying.
30.7: [God], I ask you to do two things for me; [please] do them before I die:
30.8: Help me never to lie or deceive [people] and do not cause me to become poor or to become rich. [Just] give me the food that I need;
30.9: because if I become rich, I might say that I do not know you and that I do not need you; and if I become poor, I might dishonor you by stealing things.
30.10: Do not ◄slander/say bad things about► a worker to his boss; if you do that, the worker will curse you, and cause you to have trouble.
30.11: [I will list four kinds of evil things that people do]: Some people curse their fathers and do not [ask God to] bless their mothers.
30.12: Some people think that they are perfect, but [really] they have never been cleansed from their guilt for committing disgusting sins.
30.13: Some people are very proud; they think that they are very good and they despise others.
30.14: Some people [act very cruelly toward others]; [it is as though] they have teeth that are [like] sharp knives; they severely oppress poor [people] and try to cause them to disappear from the land.
30.15: Leeches [are always wanting more blood to suck]; [similarly, greedy people are always] saying “Give [me some]!” or “Give [me more]!” There are four things that are never ◄satisfied/content with what they have►; they always want more :
30.16: The place where the dead people are; women who do not have any children; ground that needs water/rain; and a fire that always needs more wood.
30.17: Those who make fun of their fathers or refuse to obey their mothers (OR, despise their aged mothers) should [die and] have their eyes pecked out by crows, and the [rest of their corpses should be] fed to the vultures.
30.18: There are four things that are wonderful to me, [but] I do not understand any of them:
30.19: How eagles fly in the sky, how snakes [are able to] move/crawl across a big rock, how ships sail on the seas, and how a man falls in love with a woman.
30.20: This is what a woman who ◄is not faithful to/does not have sex only with► her husband does: She commits adultery , and [then] bathes and says, “I have not done anything that is wrong!”
30.21: There are four things that no [one in] the world can tolerate:
30.22: [What] a slave [does who] becomes a king, a foolish person eating [too much] food,
30.23: [what] a woman who is hated [does when she] gets married, and [what] a female servant [does when she] becomes the boss instead of her mistress.
30.24: [There are] four animals on the earth that are small, but they are very wise:
30.25: Ants are not strong, but they store up food during the summer [in order to have it during the winter].
30.26: Rock badgers [also] are not strong, but they make their homes among the rocks [where they will be safe].
30.27: Locusts do not have a king, but they march like [the soldiers in] an army.
30.28: Lizards/Geckos [are very small and] you can hold them in your hand, but they are [cleverly able to get] inside kings’ palaces.
30.29: [There are] four animals that strut around and look very impressive while they walk :
30.30: Lions, which are stronger than all other animals and are not afraid of any of them;
30.31: male goats, strutting roosters, and kings who ◄parade/walk proudly back and forth► in front of the people whom they rule.
30.32: If you have acted foolishly, exalting yourself, or if you been planning [to do something] evil, stop it immediately !
30.33: If you churn milk, it produces butter/curds, and if you hit [someone hard on his] nose, [his nose] bleeds; similarly, if you do something to cause [people to become] angry, strife [usually] results.

31.1: These are sayings/messages that [God gave to] King Lemuel’s mother, and which his mother taught him:
31.2: You are my son; I gave birth to you ; you are the son that [God gave me] in answer to my prayers.
31.3: Do not exhaust your energy [having sex] with women [to whom you are not married], with women who ruin kings [by having sex with them].
31.4: Lemuel, kings should not be [constantly] drinking wine or [greatly] desire [to drink other] strong/alcoholic drinks.
31.5: If they do that, they forget the laws [that they have made], and they do not do what is right for poor/afflicted [people].
31.6: Give strong/alcoholic drinks to those who are dying and to those who are ◄greatly distressed/suffering very much►.
31.7: If they drink, they will forget that they are poor, and they will not think about their distress/troubles any more.
31.8: Speak to defend people who are unable to defend themselves; speak to encourage others to do what is right for those who are helpless.
31.9: Speak ◄on their behalf/to help them► and try to cause judges to decide matters fairly/justly; try to cause others to do for poor and needy [people] what should be done for them.
31.10: It is very difficult [for a man] to find a wife who is good and who is capable [of doing many things]. [Any woman who is like that] is worth more than jewels.
31.11: Her husband completely trusts her, and [because of her], he has everything that he needs .
31.12: She never does anything that would harm him; she does good things for him all the days of her life.
31.13: She finds wool and flax [in the market], and she enjoys spinning it [to make yarn].
31.14: She is like a ship that brings from far away goods/merchandise to sell, [because] she buys food that comes from far away.
31.15: She gets up before dawn to prepare food for her family. [Then] she plans the work that her servant girls will do on that day.
31.16: She [goes out and] looks at a field [that someone wants to sell]; and [if it is a good field], she buys it. She [buys] grapevines with the money that she has earned, [and then] she plants them.
31.17: She works very hard ; she makes her arms strong [by the work she does].
31.18: She knows when she is getting a good profit from her business. [When it is necessary], she works until it is late at night.
31.19: She holds the ◄spindle/rod which twists the thread that she is making►, and [then] she spins the thread [that she will use].
31.20: She generously helps those who are poor and needy .
31.21: She is not worried that [the people in her house will be cold in] the winter, because [she has made] warm clothes for all of them.
31.22: She makes bedspreads/quilts for the beds. She wears fine linen clothes that are dyed purple, [like queens wear].
31.23: Her husband is [well] known by the important people of the town; he sits with the [other] town leaders in the meetings of the town council.
31.24: She makes clothes from linen cloth and sells them. She sells sashes to shop owners.
31.25: She is strong in her character and respected/dignified, and she ◄laughs at/is not afraid of► [what will happen in] the future.
31.26: When she speaks, she says what is wise. When she gives instructions, she speaks kindly (OR, faithfully).
31.27: She watches over everything that is done in her household, and she is never lazy.
31.28: Her children all together speak highly of her, and her husband also praises her.
31.29: [He says to her], “There are many women who do admirable things, but you surpass them all!”
31.30: Some women who are attractive [are not really good women], [but] they can deceive us [regarding what they are really like]. Furthermore, women’s beauty does not last; but women who revere Yahweh should be honored.
31.31: Reward women who are like that, and praise them in public for what they have done.
